info.title: reqmesh
info.description: A git-native requirements management tool with traceability, verification tracking, parametrics, and real-time collaboration.

post.description: Invalidate all of the caller's own sessions across devices.

get.description: List all accounts (without password hashes). Admins only.

post.description: Revoke every active session for a user (force sign-out everywhere).

Create an account and email a set-password link. When SMTP is not
configured the link is returned so the admin can share it manually.

Create accounts from CSV rows (username, full_name, email, role). Each new
user is invited (set-password link); existing usernames are skipped.

get.description: Build metadata for this instance (also served at /version for probes).
Return the project's workflow configuration (states, transitions, default).

post.description:
Rename a requirement, repointing children and references project-wide.

Registered before the ``/{req_id}`` catch-all for the same reason next-uid
is: otherwise "rename" is swallowed as a requirement id.

Without ``new_id`` this only *suggests* one — the parent's prefix and the
next free slot — so the dialog can prefill without a second endpoint.

``cascade`` is ``self`` (default) | ``children`` | ``descendants`` and
controls how far the new prefix reaches. ``dry_run`` returns the planned
``renames`` and the records that would be relinked without writing anything,
so the dialog can preview each choice before committing.

Rename a parameter, repointing every reference project-wide.

A parameter is addressed by its owner (a requirement or component id) and
its current name. Every ``owner.old`` / bare-name reference in expressions
and every ``[[owner.old]]`` / ``owner.old`` mention in text is rewritten,
the way the requirement and component renames rewrite their references.

get.summary: Next free id for a kind

post.description: Record a test execution run with optional step results and new status.

put.description:
Replace the trace matrix.

This is a whole-document write driven by a client-side snapshot, so two
people editing the matrix an hour apart used to mean the later save silently
erased the earlier one's links (traces have no history entry and no undo).
Send the ETag from GET as ``If-Match`` to get a 409 instead of a silent
overwrite; omitting it preserves the old last-writer-wins behaviour for
existing clients.

get.description: Every declared relationship: registry-derived edges + hand-authored traces.
Export an indented bill-of-materials as CSV.

post.description:
Rename a component, repointing children and references project-wide.

Registered before the ``/{component_id}`` catch-all for the same reason the
requirement route is: otherwise the literal ``rename`` segment can be
swallowed as a component id.

get.description: Which parts of the design claim to realise this requirement.
Which parts of the design this verification case exercises.
Effective values for every admin-editable setting (secrets redacted).

patch.description: Update runtime settings. Env-locked and blank-secret keys are ignored.

post.description: Send a test email using the current SMTP settings and report the result.

get.description: Non-sensitive instance info for the login/registration UI (no auth).
Whether a LaTeX engine is available for PDF report generation.
Runtime facts the admin UI uses to decide what update UX to show.
Latest GitHub release vs the running version. Cached; force to bypass.

post.description:
Back up data and signal the updater to move to the target version.

Uses the latest available release when target_version is omitted.

Update from an uploaded Docker image archive (offline / air-gapped).

The archive (e.g. reqmesh-vX.Y.Z-image.tar.gz from a release) is streamed to
the control volume; the sidecar then `docker load`s it and recreates the app.

Stage an uploaded release bundle for a bare-metal (non-Docker) install.

The bundle (reqmesh-vX.Y.Z.tar.gz from a release) is streamed to the
instance, validated, and staged. It's applied on the next restart — the
admin can trigger that immediately via POST /system/restart. Works offline.

Restart the app in place (re-exec). Applies any staged bundle update on
the way back up. Bare-metal only — Docker manages its own lifecycle.
Clear a completed/failed update's control files (and any staged archive).

get.description:
Whether the bundled example is present, and what re-seeding would replace.

Returns the requirement count rather than a bare boolean: "this will
overwrite 57 requirements" is a warning someone can act on, where "the
project exists" is not.

post.description:
Re-seed the bundled example, replacing whatever is there.

Admin-only, matching ``delete_project``: this is a delete followed by a
write, not a write. A 409 without ``force`` is the guard — a client that
forgets the flag gets an error rather than silently discarding the user's
work in that project.

get.description:
Aggregated audit activity bucketed by date and entity kind.

Counts **distinct item ids** per bucket per kind, not raw audit entries.
A bulk status change writes N entries in one action and would otherwise
spike a single day into the darkest bucket and dwarf every real day beside
it.

post.description:
Check that a candidate remote is reachable before it is saved.

Admin-only, matching `router._guard_git_settings`: this makes the server
perform a network (or filesystem) operation against a caller-supplied URL,
which is the same authority as setting the remote and belongs behind the
same gate. The URL is validated against the shared scheme allowlist here
*and* inside ``git_service.test_remote``.

get.description:
Return the git repository status for a project.

Performs no network access — ``ahead`` is computed against the local
remote-tracking ref so the call never hangs when the remote is unreachable.
``remote_url`` is redacted before it leaves the server.

post.description:
Initialise a git repository in the project directory.

Returns 409 if the project is already a repository.  Safe to call — the
service layer also checks for a parent repo and refuses to nest.

Push commits to the configured remote synchronously.

Commits any pending changes first so a manual push backs up the whole
working tree, not just what was already committed. Returns the real
outcome, including whether a commit was made and the redacted error on
failure. Unlike ``schedule_push``, which runs from a background timer
and logs to a file nobody reads, this route makes a broken remote
immediately diagnosable.

delete.description:
Remove the git remote *and* clear ``remote_url`` from project settings.

Admin-only: changing where a project ships its history is the same
authority as setting it, and removing a remote is a one-way operation
that stops the project from being backed up.

get.description:
The project's deploy key's public half and fingerprint, or 404.

Admin-only, matching the other admin git routes. The private key is never
returned — under any role, ever — because the moment such an endpoint
exists it is one authorisation bug away from being reachable.

post.description: Generate an ed25519 deploy keypair for the project. 409 if one exists.

delete.description: Remove the deploy key. 204 whether or not one existed.

post.description:
Replace the deploy key. The old private key is discarded.

Pushes will fail until the new public key is registered at the host — that
is the whole danger of this button, and the UI's confirmation text says so.

get.description:
Compare a frozen baseline against the current requirements or another
frozen baseline.

``name`` is always the "before" snapshot; ``against`` is the "after".
When ``against`` is absent the comparison is against the live requirements.

Read ``SRR`` against ``PDR`` as "what PDR did to SRR".

post.description:
Import requirements from a ReqIF 1.2, SysML v2 or spreadsheet file.

``format`` is ``auto`` (sniff from content), ``reqif``, ``sysml``, ``csv``,
``tsv`` or ``xlsx``.
``mode`` is ``merge`` (create/update) or ``replace`` (wipe existing first).
``dry_run`` previews the change without writing, and is available for the
table formats only.

Supply exactly one of ``file`` (uploaded file) or ``text`` (pasted content).
Pasting is supported for csv, tsv and auto only.
Assign multiple components to a new parent (set parent=None to detach).

Move selected requirements under a new parent and optionally re-prefix IDs.

With ``re_prefix`` set and the new parent's prefix differing from a moved
requirement's, that requirement and its entire descendant subtree are
renamed to the new prefix. Parent pointers and relation targets — both
inside the subtree and elsewhere in the project — are rewritten to the new
IDs so nothing is left dangling.

``dry_run`` returns the same ``renames`` the real call would perform without
writing anything, so the UI can show the rename before the user commits to
it. The planning is shared with the write path rather than reimplemented, so
the preview cannot drift from what actually happens.

get.description: Everything in the project that points at this entity, grouped by kind.
The obligation kinds a requirement may declare in ``needs``.
Severity × likelihood grid of risk counts per the project matrix.
Requirements ranked by weighted stakeholder value, best first.
The weighted stakeholder value of one requirement, and its rank.

A Pugh matrix comparing the best-valued requirements against each other,
relative to a chosen datum. Stakeholders are the criteria; their weights
scale the comparison so a heavier stakeholder moves the `weighted` total
further than a light one.
Evaluate every parameter, constraint and measurement in the project.

post.description:
Returns the evaluation with hypothetical overrides plus a
dependency-ordered trace of every parameter and constraint that
changes — so the frontend can animate the what-if cascade.

get.description: Return the users currently viewing the project (real-time roster).
Server-Sent Events stream for real-time collaboration.
Full-text search across all entity types in a project.
Requirements against components, verification cases, risks, or baselines.

post.description:
Toggle one cell of any of the allocation matrices.

The write goes to the *holder* of the link — the component, the
verification case, the risk — because that is the side the model stores.
Only ``component.satisfies`` has a persisted mirror to keep in step
(``requirement.allocated_to``); the others are recomputed on read, so
writing anything back to the requirement would create a second copy that
could disagree with the first.

The baselines axis is the exception: its membership is held by the row
entity in ``req_field``, and it stores baseline **names**, not ids.
With ``row_kind="components"`` the row entity is a component rather than
a requirement.

get.description: Return a sample JUnit XML showing the expected format for CI import.

post.description:
Import CI test results (JUnit XML, CTRF JSON, TAP) and update
verification case statuses.

get.description: Build metadata for this instance — version, git sha, build time, channel.

BulkRequest.title: BulkRequest
BulkRequest.description:
Body for a bulk update: the ids to change plus the per-kind patch.

``updates`` stays an untyped ``dict`` on purpose — the payload is
heterogeneous by design and is validated per-kind through the matching
``*Update`` model in each handler.

CRUrgency.title: CRUrgency
CRUrgency.description:
How soon the change needs deciding.

An enum rather than a per-project list, unlike the risk vocabularies: a
change request's urgency is not an axis a project configures, and CRStatus
above is already an enum, so this stays consistent with its own file.

CaseType.title: CaseType
CaseType.description: OOSEM Activity 6: verification (did we build it right?) vs validation (did we build the right thing?).

Constraint.title: Constraint
Constraint.description:
A boolean expression over parameters that must hold.

`assume` is an optional precondition: when present and not satisfied the
constraint is out of scope rather than failed (SysML assume/require).

MeasureKind.title: MeasureKind
MeasureKind.description: OOSEM measure taxonomy: MOE (operational), MOP (system), TPM (component).

Measurement.title: Measurement
Measurement.description:
A measured value recorded against a requirement parameter.

`parameter` is a fully-qualified reference (`"AFRM0005.max_load"`). The
evaluation engine substitutes these into the owning requirement's
constraints to compute a verification verdict from evidence rather than a
hand-set status.

Parameter.title: Parameter
Parameter.description:
A typed numeric quantity on a requirement or component.

Either a literal `value`, or an `expr` deriving it from other parameters
(`span * chord`, `GROS0001.mass - EMPT0001.mass`,
`rollup('WING', 'mass')`). Unlike `attributes`, these participate in
constraint evaluation.

SettingsPatch.title: SettingsPatch
SettingsPatch.description:
A flat patch of runtime-setting overrides, keyed by setting name.

Only keys declared in ``settings_store.OVERRIDABLE`` take effect; the store
coerces each value to that key's declared type and ignores unknown and
env-locked keys.
